audit.report: A replayable batch job (inventory_reconcile, pid 342823) stalled idle-in-transaction for over 4 seconds, blocking checkout sessions and degrading success to 27% over 30 seconds with $13,493/min revenue at risk. The Database Guardian proposed terminating the blocker; the Continuity Guardian requested change-calendar evidence (Invariant I2), which confirmed no active change window. After the evidence was supplied, both guardians agreed to terminate. The executor killed the session, locks cleared immediately, and checkout recovered to 100% success within the 10-second verification window.
audit.root_cause: The inventory_reconcile batch worker entered an idle-in-transaction state (last statement 'SELECT 1') and held locks that blocked all checkout sessions.
lessons: Add a statement/transaction timeout (e.g., 30s) to the inventory_reconcile job so it self-terminates instead of stalling idle-in-transaction.
Pre-load change-calendar evidence into the guardian context for batch_replayable_inventory so the Continuity Guardian does not need a revision round to satisfy Invariant I2.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian acted on complete evidence in Round 1; the Continuity Guardian correctly enforced Invariant I2 but caused a one-round delay because change-calendar data was not pre-fetched. No guardian wasted a round or missed evidence once the probe returned.
follow_ups: Implement statement_timeout and idle_in_transaction_session_timeout for the inventory_reconcile database role.
Extend the workload registry entry for batch_replayable_inventory to include change-calendar linkage so guardians receive it automatically.
Add a heartbeat metric and alert for inventory_reconcile progress to catch stalls before they impact checkout.

Memory shows a verified pact where terminating this same workload (inventory_reconcile job) restored checkout to 100% within 10s (MEM-1). The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout (BIZ-1), and we are already in that window. Waiting risks exceeding the tolerance; terminating the stuck idle-in-transaction session is the fastest path to lock release.
proposal.expected_effect: Terminating pid 342823 will release its locks immediately, unblocking the 1 waiting session (and transitively the 12 sessions waiting on locks per DB-1). Checkout success rate should recover toward 100% within seconds, as observed in the verified pact (MEM-1). The batch_replayable_inventory job (inventory_reconcile) is replayable per memory context, so interruption cost is low.
proposal.risk_assessment: Low risk: the workload is replayable (inventory_reconcile job) and was verified safe to terminate in a prior incident (MEM-1). No protected settlements are known to be held by this pid, but we will confirm via probe. The session is idle in transaction, so no active write is being interrupted.
